Hi Olga / Marissa / Kimberly,

Thanks again for taking time last week. Our legal team had a couple of follow-ups on the DPA and the technical annex. Two quick items they asked us to confirm before we move to signatures: 

1) Tenant routing / proxy: can you confirm whether requests from our tenant ever transit through a shared proxy that performs transformation/pseudonymization before reaching the model? If so, which subprocessors handle that proxy?

2) Evidence sampling for pseudonymization: for compliance we typically ask for a representative sample of pseudonymization artifacts (dataflow snapshots, redaction logs) covering the last 90 days. Can Redwood provide an itemized sampling workflow and a small sample extract we can review?

Attached is our current DPA questions list (MediRex_DPA_Q3.pdf). Legal is copied on the thread and would appreciate a short walkthrough call if helpful.

Can someone confirm timeline for answers? We are hoping to close the DPA this month.

Thanks,

Samira — thanks for the clear asks and the PDF. Looping in Connor to provide a concise technical walk-through and a diagram slice.

Quick answers up-front:
- Redwood does not route tenant inference traffic through a shared transformation proxy that alters content before model input. Customers may deploy optional edge proxies in front of our inference endpoints, but those are customer-managed unless they opt into Redwood-managed connectors (which we list as subprocessors).
- We can provide a sampling workflow for pseudonymization artifacts and 90-day samples for logs/exports where applicable. There are tradeoffs for live production telemetry (privacy of other tenants) so we usually provide redacted extracts and attestations plus pipeline snapshots.

Connor — can you attach the tenant-routing sketch and a proposed sampling checklist? Also please call out which subprocessors touch telemetry or routing for a managed connector scenario.

Timeline: we can turn around initial artifacts within 48 business hours and schedule a 30-min walkthrough tomorrow if that works for MediRex.

—Olga
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attached: tenant-routing-diagram.svg (svg, 45KB)

Folks — notes and proposed artifact set for MediRex: 

Summary (short):
- Default hosted mode: tenant requests go directly to Redwood front-end load balancers, then to tenant-scoped inference pools. No shared content-modifying proxy is in-line.
- Managed connectors (opt-in): when customers ask for Redwood-managed connectors (ingest helpers, formatters), those are supported by dedicated subprocessors; connectors perform optional normalization, not pseudonymization unless configured.

Subprocessor list relevant to routing/telemetry (managed connector path):
- EdgeWorks Inc. (connector orchestration)
- LogHarbor LLC (ingest telemetry retention & indexing)
- QuantizeOps (quantization/packaging for model variants)

Pseudonymization / redaction approach:
- We support redaction rules at ingestion (regex-based or field mapping) executed either client-side, in the connector, or as a pre-processing layer controlled by the customer.
- For Redwood-managed pre-processing, we produce redaction logs (timestamps, rule id, record hash) stored in our evidence store for 90 days by default; samples can be exported as CSV with sensitive payloads redacted.

Evidence sampling workflow (proposed):
1) Identify scope (tenant IDs, time window).
2) Create redaction-log export (hashed IDs only) and a dataflow snapshot (ingest → connector → inference pool).
3) Apply additional redactions (remove all PII values), produce attestations signed by our Privacy Ops.
4) Deliver sample artifacts + chain-of-custody statement.

Retention exceptions & approvals:
- Standard: telemetry metadata + redaction logs retained 90 days.
- Exceptions: customers can request extended retention via support ticket and an approved SOW/Annex; approvals require Legal + Privacy Ops sign-off.

Open question for MediRex: do you plan to use Redwood-managed connectors or operate client-side normalization? If client-side, subprocessors for routing are not in-scope.

Connor O
Product Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Legal also asked whether Redwood can support an on-prem evidence transfer (SCP or secure SFTP) for the sample package instead of sending via shared cloud links. Please cc our Legal ops (legal@medirex.com) on any transfer plans.

Would you be able to provide a minimally redacted sample bundle for review by tomorrow EOD PST?

Regards,
